paperName: The National Economy in a Global Context

questions.questionText: When an economy goes into a recession, there is most likely to be a

options.text: growing balance of payments deficit.
positive output gap.
reduction in real GDP.
rise in inflation.

questions.questionText: Economic growth in the US increases from 2% to 5% a year. This is most likely to represent for the UK a

options.text: negative demand-side shock.
negative supply-side shock.
positive demand-side shock.
positive supply-side shock.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a true statement about the Labour Force Survey (LFS) measure of unemployment? The LFS measure of unemployment includes

options.text: part-time workers who would like to work full-time.
people who are claiming unemployment benefits.
people who would like a job but who are not currently looking for one.
students at university searching for a job starting after they have graduated.

questions.questionText: The table shows income and expenditure on goods and services for four workers for the tax year ending April 2018. The government has set a proportional income tax rate of 25% and a tax on all expenditure of 15%. Which one of the following statements is true? During the tax year ending April 2018 the

options.text: burden of total tax, measured as a percentage of income, was highest for Jennie.
gap in income between Meshaal and Thavid remained the same before and after paying income tax.
tax on expenditure was not regressive as all four workers faced the same rate of tax.
worker who made the greatest contribution to government tax revenue was Alice.

questions.questionText: The government of an economy implements an expansionary fiscal policy, increasing government spending and cutting taxes. In the short run, such a policy is likely to result in a conflict between which of the following macroeconomic objectives?

options.text: Increasing economic growth and reducing unemployment.
Preventing deflation and reducing the surplus on the current account of the balance of payments.
Preventing deflation and reducing unemployment.
Reducing the deficit on the current account of the balance of payments and increasing economic growth.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the multiplier effect of an increase in investment that at first causes aggregate demand (AD) to shift from AD0 to AD1 and subsequently to AD2. Which one of the following shows the size of the multiplier effect that has occurred?

options.text: Y0 Y1 divided by Y0 Y2
Y0 Y2 divided by Y0 Y1
Y0 Y2 divided by Y1 Y2
Y1 Y2 divided by Y0 Y1

extractionNotes: the question prints a diagram or chart (an image)
19 subscript or superscript glyph(s) set flush against their base

questions.questionText: Many firms use profits to finance their capital investment instead of borrowing from banks. For these firms, higher interest rates are most likely to

options.text: cause them to change the type of investment made with more investment in buildings.
cause them to reduce their investment as they can now earn more interest from saving their profits.
have no impact on the amount of investment undertaken as they pay no interest.
result in more investment as they can earn more interest on money deposited in banks.

questions.questionText: There is a large depreciation in an economy’s exchange rate but the value of its exports does not increase. The most likely reason for the absence of an increase in the value of exports is that

options.text: consumer confidence in the economy has fallen.
other countries are in recession.
the government has implemented contractionary fiscal policy.
there is an increase in unemployment in the economy.

questions.questionText: The table below shows a selection of items from a country’s balance of payments on current account. If the country has a current account deficit of £84 billion, its balance of trade in services has a

options.text: deficit of £13 billion.
deficit of £40 billion.
surplus of £13 billion.
surplus of £40 billion.

extractionNotes: 4 line(s) of figure or table text printed with the question are not reproduced; see the question paper

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements about supply-side policies and supply-side improvements is true?

options.text: Supply-side improvements do not affect the balance of payments on current account
Supply-side improvements often originate in the private sector
Supply-side policies have no impact on the budget balance
Supply-side policies work by leaving incentives unchanged

questions.questionText: In the diagram below, as a result of the government implementing a new industrial policy, the long-run aggregate supply curve shifts from LRAS1 to LRAS2 The shift in LRAS suggests that the industrial policy is most likely to have

options.text: caused firms to be more innovative.
created a positive output gap.
reduced employment and inflation.
reduced imports and exports.

questions.questionText: An economy is in macroeconomic equilibrium with total expenditure and total income each equal to £407 billion. This means that the current value of total output will be

options.text: £407 billion plus the annual rate of economic growth.
£814 billion after adjusting for the multiplier effect.
the same as total expenditure and total income.
the same as total income after adjusting for inflation.

questions.questionText: A government wanting to reduce unemployment in the short run, through the use of fiscal policy, is most likely to

options.text: attempt to increase the size of its budget surplus.
reduce indirect taxes on consumption.
reduce interest rates to stimulate investment.
take measures to reduce the size of its budget deficit.

questions.questionText: World oil prices rise by 30%. On an AD/AS diagram the main effects are shown by a shift left in

options.text: both the aggregate demand curve and the short-run aggregate supply curve.
the aggregate demand curve as consumers face higher prices for petrol.
the long-run aggregate supply curve as firms reduce their investment in renewable energy.
the short-run aggregate supply curve as firms face higher costs.

questions.questionText: The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of England has to assess inflationary pressures when deciding on the level of Bank Rate. Which one of the following pieces of information is most likely to persuade the Committee to raise Bank Rate?

options.text: A fall in the number of job vacancies advertised
GDP growth at below the trend rate in the previous two quarters
Statistics showing an increase in bank lending to households
Surveys showing that many firms have spare capacity

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand curves (AD) and short-run aggregate supply curves (SRAS) for an economy. Which one of the following combinations of events is most likely to have caused the shift from AD1 to AD2 and the shift from SRAS1 to SRAS2?

options.text: A fall in commodity prices and a fall in savings
A fall in money wages and an increase in imports
An increase in the budget deficit and a fall in productivity
An increase in VAT and an increase in income tax

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sets of circumstances is most likely, other things remaining the same, to lead to demand-pull and cost-push inflation in an economy?

options.text: A depreciation in the exchange rate, and a reduction in the government’s budget surplus
Labour productivity growth in the economy accelerates, and interest rates fall
The minimum wage is increased, and business confidence in the economy falls
World demand for commodities increases, and the economy’s trade surplus becomes smaller

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand curve (AD), short-run aggregate supply curve (SRAS), and long-run aggregate supply curve (LRAS) for an economy. The current level of real GDP is Y. Which one of the following policies is most likely, in the short run, to bring the economy closer to its normal capacity level of output?

options.text: An increase in the target rate of inflation
Higher government spending on vocational education
Lower rates of tax on manufacturing businesses
New schemes to encourage more household saving
